content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper presents a Hybrid Neural Representation for Videos (HNeRV), where learnable and content-adaptive embeddings
act as the decoder input. Besides the input embedding, the paper additionally introduces an HNeRV block to make model parameters evenly distributed across the entire network, therefore higher layers (layers near the output) can have more capacity to store high-resolution content and video details. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of HNeRV on downstream tasks such as video compression and video inpainting.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The research problem is interesting. The idea is interesting.
2. HNeRV outperforms implicit methods (NeRV, E-NeRV) in video regression task for both reconstruction quality and convergence speed, and shows better internal generalization.
3. HNeRV also shows decoding advantages for speed, flexibility, and deployment, compared to traditional codecs (H.264, H.265) and learning-based compression methods.
4. HNeRV shows impressive results on down-stream video compression and inpainting tasks.
5. The paper is well organized.

Weakness:
1. The paper includes many typos and detailed issues. 
For example, "learnabl" should be "learnable", "a HNeRV" should be "an HNeRV"
The author should carefully double-check all details of the paper.
2. The proposed method is not compared with SOTA compression and inpainting methods.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper studied the task of neural representation for videos, where a hybrid neural representation (HNeRV) is proposed to combine the advantages of both explicit and implicit methods. 

With content-adaptive embedding (the video frame is taken as the input) and evenly-distributed parameters, HNeRV improves video regression performance compared to implicit methods (the frame index is taken as the only input) in reconstruction quality, convergence speed, and internal generalization. HNeRV is simple, fast, and flexible for video decoding, and shows good performance for video compression and inpainting.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength：

+ A hybrid neural representation (HNeRV) is proposed to combine the advantages of both explicit (using an auto-encoder to encode and decode all videos, and store content explicitly as a latent embedding) and implicit methods (using only a learnable decoder to represent the video). 

+ With content-adaptive embedding and evenly-distributed parameters, HNeRV improves video regression performance compared to implicit methods in reconstruction quality, convergence speed, and internal generalization

Weaknesses：

- The proposed hybrid neural representation is a mixture of existing methods (implicit and explicit), in this way, the real technical novelty is to some extent limited.

- The current implicit, explicit and the proposed hybrid approches learns the video representation in a frame-by-frame manner, where the essentials of video are lost. In particular, a video is not a simple a collections of image frames but has strong temporal coorelation. I would like to see more in-depth studies in the learned video representation, where the concept of video has been learned.

- The paper claimed the "evenly-distributed parameters" as a major contribution. Further analysis, visualziation and studies are needed to valiadate this point and its relevance for video representation.

- The language should be improved. Currently there are grammar and spelling errors across the paper such as "where learnabl" and "For quantization of an vector"

- Further ablation studies should be provided for different loss functions.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is basicall written in a clear way.

Quality: The quality of the paper is in general OK but could be improved. Please address my major concerns as listed above in the paper weaknesses section.

Novelty: The technial novelty seems to be incremental and the ablation studies tend to insufficient.

Reproducibility: The paper has provided much of the details to re-implement the proposed method. Release of the code will help.

HNeRV improves video regression performance compared to implicit methods (the frame index is taken as the only input) in reconstruction quality, convergence speed, and internal generalization. The proposed hybrid neural representation is a mixture of existing methods (implicit and explicit), in this way, the real technical novelty is to some extent limited. My major concerns also lie in whether the concept of video has really been learned within the neural representation.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, authors design a hybrid neural representation for videos. By conditioning implicit representation models such as NeRV on additional input of content-adaptive video embedding, the proposed method has more capacity in storing high-resolution details of videos. Authors also find that making model parameters evenly distributed over both early and later stages is beneficial to video decoding process. The proposed method is shown to perform better than NeRV in video regression tasks. The proposed method can also be extended to several downstream tasks such as video compression and video inpainting.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
1. Authors show the benefits of having content-adaptive video embedding as additional input to the implicit representation model. It can obtain better decoding performance with little increase on model size.
2. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The proposed method shows faster inference speed than both traditional methods and learning-based methods. The proposed method performs better than other implicit representation methods such as NeRV and E-NeRV in terms of both reconstruction performance on different resolution of videos.

Cons:
1. Novelty issue. Novelty is quite limited. The proposed HNeRV is quite similar to NeRV. The proposed HNeRV only adds video-specific latent embedding as additional input for NeRV. The proposed HNeRV block is also not novel in terms of network architecture design.
2. Fig. 1 (a) and (b) are not informative. They do not clearly show difference between implicit neural representation and hybrid neural representation.
3. English writing should be further improved.
4. formats of reference are messy.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Overall, the novelty of this work only has incremental novelty on top of NeRV. The english writing also needs improvement.
Overall I do not think the submission at current state is ready for publication.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall I do not think the submission at current state is ready for publication on this conference.
